primary_source.title: AblateCell: A Reproduce-then-Ablate Agent for Virtual Cell Repositories

verdict.summary: The candidate's core reproduce-then-ablate mechanism and headline numbers are present in the primary paper. Full-paper inspection materially strengthens evidence for specific internal modules, especially adaptive search, but does not isolate the causal value of the reproduce-first ordering itself. The human-comparator and critical-component-ground-truth semantics require narrower wording than the headline abstract suggests.

verified_claims.claim: AblateCell first reproduces repository baselines and only then runs closed-loop isolated ablations selected under a performance-impact versus cost objective.
verified_claims.scope: Three public virtual-cell repositories: CPA, GEARS, BioLORD. The paper explicitly says it starts from runnable baseline repositories and is not a paper-to-code reconstruction benchmark.

verified_claims.claim: End-to-end workflow success is 88.9%, reported as +29.9 percentage points over the paper's Human Experts row.
verified_claims.scope: Table 1 averages BioLORD, GEARS and CPA; Human Experts average is 59.0 and AblateCell is 88.9. This is the paper's comparator protocol, not a general autonomous-agent-versus-unaided-human effect.

verified_claims.claim: Component identification reaches 93.3% Acc@5, +53.3 percentage points over heuristic-based selection.
verified_claims.scope: Table 2: heuristic-based Acc@5=40.0; AblateCell with Claude-Sonnet-4.5=93.3. The metric is top-5 overlap against expert-consensus ground truth within the paper's reduced candidate component space.

verified_claims.claim: Verified reproduction requires more than execution success.
verified_claims.scope: Appendix B.2.1 states that reproduced baselines must both execute autonomously and match original-paper primary metrics within +/-5% relative error, using repository-default configurations without extra hyperparameter tuning.

verified_claims.claim: Ground-truth critical components are expert validated.
verified_claims.scope: Three independent PhD-level domain experts per repository rank components after reviewing ablation results; criticality also requires at least 5% relative primary-metric change. Reported agreement is Fleiss kappa 0.72 for criticality and 82.7% average pairwise top-5 overlap. This is an expert/empirical hybrid reference, not exhaustive objective ground truth over all repository mechanisms.

new_primary_source_findings.finding: The full paper contains matched system ablations that the source checkpoint had not yet incorporated.
new_primary_source_findings.evidence: Full system: TSR 88.9, Acc@5 93.3. Without planner-executor: TSR 65.4, Acc@5 89.7. Without domain knowledge: TSR 70.2, Acc@5 70.0. Without adaptive bandit: TSR 88.1, Acc@5 53.3. Without Git worktree: TSR/Acc@5 unchanged at 88.9/93.3 while time rises 45.2 to 78.5 minutes.
new_primary_source_findings.implication: The adaptive search policy has direct matched evidence for component-identification quality, and planner-executor has direct matched evidence for execution reliability. The prior checkpoint's limitation remains valid only for the narrower claim that no matched row removes the reproduce-first sequencing/gate itself while holding the downstream ablation machinery fixed.

new_primary_source_findings.finding: The candidate component universe is pre-filtered rather than exhaustive.
new_primary_source_findings.evidence: The paper reports 12 CPA, 15 GEARS and 9 BioLORD components after hybrid extraction/knowledge-base validation, with manual removal of 2-3 clearly non-ablatable components per repository; bandit search then navigates mutation configurations without exhaustive enumeration.
new_primary_source_findings.implication: 93.3% Acc@5 should be phrased as recovery of expert-consensus top-5 components within this constructed candidate space, not discovery of 93.3% of all truly critical mechanisms in the repositories.

new_primary_source_findings.finding: The human-comparator semantics are internally awkward and should not be generalized.
new_primary_source_findings.evidence: Section 4.2 describes six human experts independently reproducing baselines and designing ablations under closed-book conditions, two hours per task and up to five debug attempts. Appendix C.2 also states that all methods, explicitly including human experts, use GPT-4o with identical generation hyperparameters. The paper additionally gives AblateCell a pre-built domain knowledge base not available to Mini-SWE-Agent or RepoMaster.
new_primary_source_findings.implication: The +29.9pp number is source-correct as a table difference but does not cleanly identify an architecture-only or unaided-human causal advantage. Preserve it only as 'versus the paper's Human Experts condition'.

unverified_or_not_supported.claim: The reproduce-first ordering itself causally improves attribution accuracy versus an otherwise identical ablation agent that skips reproduction.
unverified_or_not_supported.reason: No matched system-ablation row was found that removes only the reproduce-first ordering while preserving the same mutation graph, search policy, knowledge and execution stack.

unverified_or_not_supported.claim: The reported results establish wet-lab or broader autonomous-science discovery yield.
unverified_or_not_supported.reason: All three evaluated targets are computational single-cell repositories.

unverified_or_not_supported.claim: Independent reproduction of AblateCell's full reported experiment from released code/artifacts.
unverified_or_not_supported.reason: This was a primary-source semantic/quantitative verification pass, not a reproduction audit; no official AblateCell implementation repository was established in this pass.

termination.exact_next_verification: Fresh-bootstrap on the then-current main/control tuple. Rotate away from AblateCell unless a released official implementation/artifact materially changes reproducibility status. Next prioritize an under-audited named-source scientist_agents claim with a quantitative or mechanistic assertion; preserve candidate_095's remaining narrow open question as whether any primary experiment directly ablates the reproduce-first ordering itself.
